note: Orders every 2 days (even days) covering two days of forecast ×1.07 plus a starting buffer; this saves about half the fixed fees. Main risk: shortages on high-demand days without a daily top-up.
2-day cycle on odd days with a separate start-up order on day 0, so both spikes (days 17 and 25) land in their own deliveries. Main risk: one extra fee, and the same exposure to demand noise.
3-day cycle (about 10 fees) with a separate order for the item-1 spike on day 25. Main risk: hitting the 220-unit warehouse cap around days 16–17 and more holding cost.
2-day cycle with a high safety margin (×1.2); shortage penalties are higher than the cost of a surplus. Main risk: surplus piling up, write-offs and leftovers at the end.
2-day cycle ordering at the forecast mean with no buffer. Main risk: frequent shortages and penalties, especially for item 1.
Daily orders of the arrival day's forecast ×1.05 plus a starting buffer; this follows the forecast closely. Main risk: about 1000 in fixed fees.
Daily orders at ×1.2 of forecast. Main risk: all the fees plus a steady build-up of surplus and item-0 write-offs.
Lean daily orders at ×0.95 of forecast. Main risk: lost sales and penalties, since actual demand averages about 5% above forecast.
